name: com.handshakr/handshakr
title: Handshakr
description: Read-only search of Handshakr's register of B2B suppliers, a record built for AI buying agents.

tools.name: search_sellers
tools.description: Search the Handshakr suppliers an AI agent may read, by keyword, optionally narrowed by the register's three classifications: `category` (what they do: a top category slug such as 'software-engineering', or a subcategory), `industry` (who it's for, e.g. 'legal-technology') and `delivery` ('software', 'services' or 'hardware'), combined with AND. A classification only narrows the results; it never changes which supplier comes first (contactable first, then by name). Returns name, slug, category, location, description, `contactable` (true only for suppliers who have switched agent access on, the only ones an agent may approach) and `classification`: { what_they_do, who_its_for, delivery } each { slug, top_slug, name, method, method_label, source } or null with `unknown_reason` saying why, and `taxonomy_version`. `method` is supplier, label, sic (Companies House SIC code) or website (their own website text, not reviewed). Claimed suppliers who have not consented are not returned. `description` and `category` are the company's own words or null; text Handshakr wrote from public sources is in `handshakr_summary` / `handshakr_category`, labelled, and is not a fact about the company. `trust_score` is null: no score is computed.

query.description: Search term matched against seller name and description.

category.description: Optional. What they do: a category slug (e.g. 'software-engineering', 'it-services', or a subcategory such as 'managed-it-services'). A value that is not a category slug is matched against the listing's category label instead, as before.

industry.description: Optional. Who it's for: an industry slug (e.g. 'legal-technology', 'healthcare-life-sciences').

delivery.description: Optional. How it is delivered: software, services or hardware.

limit.description: Maximum number of suppliers to return (1 to 50, default 10).

tools.name: get_seller
tools.description: Fetch one Handshakr supplier an AI agent may read, by slug. `contactable` says whether the supplier has switched agent access on and may be approached. `description` and `category` are the company's own words or null; text Handshakr wrote from public sources is in `handshakr_summary` / `handshakr_category`, labelled, and is not a fact about the company. `trust_score` is null: no score is computed. `trading_name_of`, when not null, names the registered company this listing is a trading name of (legal name, company number, the passport holding its Companies House record): listings that share a company number there are one company, not several. `verifiable_record` is the latest signed, append-only version of the public passport: its version, sha256, log position, and where to fetch the W3C Verifiable Credential and its status. `classification` is the register's three classifications: { what_they_do, who_its_for, delivery } each { slug, top_slug, name, method, method_label, source } or null with `unknown_reason` saying why, and `taxonomy_version`; `method` is supplier, label, sic (Companies House SIC code) or website (their own website text, not reviewed). `register_checks` lists what public sources said on a date (DNS, TLS, security.txt, GLEIF, ICO, SEC EDGAR): observations, not claims; `not_checked` means nothing observed yet, and sanctions appear only as `no_match` against all four lists. Each is null when it could not be read.

tools.name: get_public_pulse
tools.description: Recent public activity in the Handshakr register: suppliers newly published and source pulse events. Only suppliers an AI agent may read are named.

limit.description: How many recent events to return (1 to 100, default 25).

tools.name: get_trending_categories
tools.description: Top trending supplier categories among the suppliers an AI agent may read, this week vs last week, with delta percentage. Returns available:false with a reason when too few recently published profiles are categorised to compute a trend, an empty result is never a silent zero.

limit.description: How many categories to return (1 to 30, default 8).
